=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:735-740 (applied at line 796) | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: CREDENTIAL_HANDOFF_RE does not catch a credentials step that names another repository by an `OWNER/REPO` slug (e.g. `gh secret set GH_PAT --repo acme/consumer-app`), so `_observable_condition` returns ("credentials", []).
  WHY: `_check_credentials` only checks this repository's own workflow runs, so the tick can mark the step done and `_close_tracker_when_done` can close the tracker while the other repository's secret is unset. Reviewers disagreed on severity: minimax rated it NIT, the others MAJOR, so the highest is used. openai_gpt-6-luna reported this together with the "in" and "repository" gaps in one finding with confidence 5.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:735-740 (applied at line 796) | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The first alternative of CREDENTIAL_HANDOFF_RE only matches `to|for|with|from`, so handoff wording that uses `in`, `into`, `at`, `via` or `by` (e.g. "Set GH_PAT in the vendor's portal") is classified as observable credentials.
  WHY: Any recent successful run of a listed workflow in this repository counts as proof, so the step is ticked "Done" and the tracker can close while the human handoff is still undone. All reviewers rated it MAJOR.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:737-738 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The second alternative `(?:consumer|other|every|each|all)\s+repo` reportedly requires exactly `repo`, so phrasings such as "consumer repository", "consumer repositories" or "every customer repos" get past the handoff filter.
  WHY: The tick would mark the step done and could close the tracker while the consumer secret is unset. The claim is disputed: anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash state that the alternative has no trailing boundary and does match "repository".
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:738 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The third alternative `(send|email|share|forward|hand\s+(?:over|off))` matches anywhere in the text without handoff context, so legitimate credential steps that mention e.g. "email support@github.com" are flagged as unrecognised.
  WHY: This fails closed: an observable entry is never ticked by the daily tick and waits for the promote cycle. Both reviewers rated it NIT.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:836-858 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `_check_credentials` returns "met" as soon as one workflow has a recent successful run, before it reaches the `"error"` → "check_failed" fallback, so a failed read of another workflow is silently ignored.
  WHY: Reviewers disagreed on severity: gemini rated it MAJOR, minimax NIT, noting it matches the documented contract but differs from `_check_allow_auto_merge`/`_check_stable_release`. The highest is used. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash judge it intended, by-design behaviour.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:834-858 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: A failed or unreadable workflow-runs API read is cached as `"error"`, but `_check_credentials` returns "not_met" instead of failing closed with "check_failed".
  WHY: During a transient GitHub outage the check would conclude "not met" instead of signalling a failure. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash state this is already fixed (line 856 / lines 850-857 return "check_failed").
- scripts/operator_step_daily_tick.sh:52-54 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `git fetch ... >/dev/null 2>&1` failure is only warned about (fail-open).
  WHY: A failed fetch can cause `stable_sha` resolution failures or `_is_ancestor` calls with missing objects, leaving entries open indefinitely instead of signalling a check failure.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "any other UPPER_SNAKE name, rotate/revoke/scope/expire/permission wording or a human-object word outside the condition's own vocabulary makes the step unrecognised" — the contract docs listing the unrecognised triggers do not include the new credential-handoff trigger (CREDENTIAL_HANDOFF_RE)
  expected_change_site: agents.d/10118-operator-step-daily-tick.md classification sentence; README.md:3126 `OPERATOR_STEP_DAILY_TICK_ENABLED` row; changelog.d/10118-operator-step-daily-tick.md bullet 4
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: CREDENTIAL_HANDOFF_RE was added at scripts/operator_step_issue.py:735-740 (applied at :796), but the agents.d/, README.md and changelog.d/ diffs have no matching wording, agents.md:2 and changelog.d:5 still lack a handoff clause, the last-run diff touched only scripts/operator_step_issue.py and tests/test_operator_step_issue.py, and a grep for "handoff" in the three docs finds no mention
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:CREDENTIAL_HANDOFF_RE (lines 735-740) and its use in `_observable_condition` (line 796, `if condition == "credentials" and CREDENTIAL_HANDOFF_RE.search(text): return None`); the proof comes from `_check_credentials` (lines 834-858). | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The handoff guard misses an explicit `--repo OWNER/REPO` slug naming another repository (e.g. "gh secret set GH_PAT --repo acme/consumer-app"), so `_observable_condition` returns ("credentials", []).
  WHY: `_check_credentials` only queries the tick's own repository, so a recent `review_autofix.yml` success returns "met", the done marker is posted, and `_close_tracker_when_done` may close the tracker. Entries are model-written (`scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1763` upsert). The test fixture only covers the same-repo slug (tests/test_operator_step_issue.py:15). Suggested fix: pass `repo` into `_observable_condition` and return None on a differing `--repo`/`-R` slug, plus a parametrized test.
- Other categories: NONE. The reviewer rejected the claim that "Set it in the consumer repository" slips past the guard (the `repo` alternative matches the "repository" prefix). It also rejected the gemini `_check_credentials` findings: line 856 returns "check_failed", and "met" taking precedence is intended. It reported no task gaps (all Phase 9 files are present, and the doc-handoff gap is not a requirement of the linked issue).
- Hardening suggestions (2 related items), HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3: (1) treat a `--repo`/`-R` slug that differs from `repo` as a handoff in the credentials branch near line 796 (6-8 lines). (2) Extend the line 736 preposition alternation to `(?:to|for|with|from|in|into|at|via)` (1 line).
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

  PROBLEM: The first alternative only matches `to|for|with|from`, so `in`/`into`/`at`/`via`/`by` handoffs (e.g. "Set GH_PAT in the vendor's portal") return ("credentials", []).
  WHY: The step is ticked "Done: ..." and `_close_tracker_when_done` can close the tracker as completed.

  PROBLEM: Requires exactly `repo`, so `repository`/`repositories`/`repos` phrasings slip past, and HUMAN_OBJECT_TITLE_RE does not catch them either.
  WHY: The tick marks the step done and may close the tracker while the consumer secret is unset.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:lines 735-740 (CREDENTIAL_HANDOFF_RE) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: No `OWNER/REPO` slug pattern, so `gh secret set GH_PAT --repo acme/consumer-app` or "Set GH_PAT for owner/consumer" gets past the guard.
  WHY: `_check_credentials` proves the credential only in this repository, so the tracker may close while the other repository's secret is unset.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:line 738 (third alternative `(send|email|share|forward|hand\s+(?:over|off))`) | severity=NIT | confidence=3

  WHY: The entry is not ticked and logs `outcome=unrecognised reason=` even though it is observable.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:lines 839-858 (_check_credentials) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The loop returns `met` before the `any(cache.get(...) == "error")` → `check_failed` fallback.
  WHY: This is a design observation: it honours the documented contract, but a failed read is silent, which differs from `_check_allow_auto_merge`/`_check_stable_release`.
